title: Starter SDKs: Opinionated flow and checklist (draft)
content:
Overview:
This is a working draft of a pragmatic, opinionated starter experience for Redwood SDKs. Goal: a 3–8 minute "first success" path for new engineers integrating Redwood, plus a short suite of follow-on micro-labs that teach common production patterns (streaming, tool-calls, usage telemetry, embeddings).

Audience:
- Software engineers evaluating Redwood for a new product feature
- Platform engineers looking to embed Redwood as a standard service
- Developer advocates creating sample apps and workshops

Why opinionated?
We have many possible knobs (HTTP vs. SDK, streaming vs. sync, modeling choices, token vs. function outputs). For first-time users we should reduce choices to a single recommended flow that is easy to teach, test, and measure. Later docs/labs can cover variations.

Top-level success metric (MVP):
- 60% of users who open the quickstart complete the hello-world lab in <=10 minutes on first try (measured via quickstart telemetry + completion ping).
- 75% of completed labs trigger at least one follow-up sample (embedding or streaming) within 7 days.

Opinionated first-run flow (three steps) — CLI-first, repo scaffold, run:  
1) Install: curl|npm|pip one-liner that creates a local scaffold.
   - Example (pseudo):
     curl https://dl.redwood.ai/init | bash && cd redwood-hello && redwood dev
   - Outcome: a folder with minimal README, .env.example, 3 short files: main.py (or index.js), prompts.md, tests/test_quickstart.py
2) Run: single command to start a dev server that connects to hosted API with test creds (auto-populated from free credits or local sandbox).
   - redwood run --dev  (starts local dev app and opens example UI at http://localhost:3000)
3) Inspect & iterate: change the prompt in prompts.md, rerun, observe streaming tokens in UI and test assertions passing.

Why CLI-first?
- Shortcut for non-frontend engineers (avoids manual project wiring).
- Gives us a single telemetry hook to track completion and failures.
- Easier to provide baked-in tests that run in CI for SDK regressions.

Micro-labs (next steps after hello-world) — short, isolated exercises (10–20 minutes each):
- Lab A: Streaming & partial-rendering (show streaming in UI; measure latency).
- Lab B: Embeddings quick: index 50 docs, run a vector search by query.
- Lab C: Function/tool calling: wire a simple tool for math or calendar lookup, return structured JSON.
- Lab D: Error & retry patterns: simulate 502/429, show retry/backoff settings and graceful fallback to smaller model.
- Lab E: Cost-aware batching demo: local simulation of traffic and switch between batching policy presets.

Minimal learning checks (automated):
- Test 1: quickstart smoke test (app starts, API call succeeds).
- Test 2: streaming output contains expected prefix string.
- Test 3: embedding vector dims match model spec and search returns >0 hits.
(These are runnable pytest / jest tests included in scaffold.)

Developer console walkthrough (what to show in docs):
- Token usage by endpoint (show how to inspect per-route token breakdown).
- Latency timeline (where time is spent: network vs. model vs. queuing).
- How to toggle between 'dev sandbox' and real tenant credentials.

Telemetry & privacy notes (short):
- Quickstart should send a single anonymized completion ping (no user code or prompts) stating which labs completed.
- Opt-out: environment variable REDWOOD_ANALYTICS=0 disables pings.

Experiment matrix (what to A/B test in beta):
- CLI vs. raw SDK onboarding: completion rate and time-to-success.
- One-liner scaffold vs. manual instructions.
- Streaming visible by default vs. off (does streaming increase perceived success?).

Checklist for engineering handoff (what needs to be implemented):
- [ ] CLI scaffolding: init templates for Python/Node/Go minimal apps.
- [ ] Local dev server that proxies to sandbox endpoints and simulates rate limits.
- [ ] Built-in tests in scaffold; CI job template for verifying SDK changes.
- [ ] Quick telemetry ping and dashboard to monitor completion funnels.
- [ ] Sample app UI components (streaming token renderer, embedding search box).
- [ ] Docs page + short video (90–120s) demonstrating the 3-step flow.

Docs tone and structure (recommendation):
- Keep first page extremely short: 3 bullets = what it does, one command to run, one screenshot.
- Deeper sections for each micro-lab with explicit learning outcomes and test assertions.
- Insert short "notes to reviewers" blocks in the draft that state assumptions (e.g., which model is the default).

Edge cases / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Auth UX for enterprise users (SAML + key provisioning) — out of scope for initial quickstart, but we need a documented path in a follow-up doc.
- What credential seed do we hand out for self-serve? (free credits vs. sandbox token that expires).
- Should the CLI attempt to auto-open firewall ports for private deployments? Likely no — add a manual step.

Sample copy for landing readme (short):
- "Welcome — run one command to open a local demo that shows Redwood generating text, streaming, and a sample embedding search. No config required for sandbox mode."

Rollout plan for internal beta:
- Week 0: implement scaffold + tests + telemetry.
- Week 1: invite 20 internal devs across product, infra, and SRE; measure completion + notes collection.
- Week 2: iterate docs and CLI based on feedback.
- Week 3: open to public self-serve with highlighted 'Report issue' flow that tags devx.

Notes for the Developer Advocates (what to prepare):
- Two live recordings: 3-minute demo & 15-minute deeper lab walkthrough.
- One workshop deck with 4 exercises mapped to micro-labs.

Next steps (concrete):
- Aiden: prototype CLI scaffold (alpha) by 2025-03-18.
- Priya: draft quick landing page copy + 90s demo script by 2025-03-11.
- Lina: add telemetry dashboard skeleton to Grafana by 2025-03-25.
- Ethan: write CI tests for the scaffold and add to staging pipeline by 2025-03-22.

Quick links (internal):
- GH starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter
- Tracking ticket: ENG-1287
- Discussion thread: slack://channel/devx-onboarding/thread/GB12345

TODO (short):
- Flesh out Python and JS sample code with clear minimal error handling.
- Create a small embedding dataset (50 entries) for the embedding lab.
- Decide default model for quickstart (latency-minimized small LLM vs. high-quality medium LLM).

End of draft — this doc is intentionally terse and action-focused. Add comments inline or drop suggestions directly in the GH PR linked above.
